journal_lines: A pack emerged from the tree line. Did not run. Neither did they. When the moon moved, both groups went their separate ways.
Yellow eyes in the dark. Held the ground. They held theirs. Eventually the night settled it.
Territorial. Both of us. Stood until one side lost interest. Was not us.
Read their leader's eyes. Their leader read mine. Nothing happened. Nothing needed to.
Six of them, three of us. Counted twice. The math did not change anything that needed changing.
An old wolf among them, scarred along the muzzle. Nodded to him. He nodded back. Wolves can do this.
The standoff lasted until the wind shifted. The wind chose for us.
Stood very still. The pack stood very still. The trees did the work of being trees.
